text:
Lena: Observed a streaming endpoint hang in our Android sample-app. App starts a flow that collects lines from an SSE-like chunked response; after ~2 minutes the coroutine waiting on collect() never resumes even though server closed the stream.
Marco: Any exceptions in logs? Socket closed events?
Lena: No stacktrace. OkHttp shows the call as "executed" but no onFailure/onResponse callbacks after server close. Happens on API 30 emulator and some devices.
Jun: My guess: mix of readTimeout vs callTimeout semantics + retrofit suspend adapters. If you only set readTimeout and the server closes the stream, but the suspend wrapper is waiting on response body buffered reads, the coroutine may not be resumed if cancel wiring is incorrect. Also OkHttp added Call.timeout() API in 3.12+ to do per-call deadlines; older code relying on client-level readTimeout can leave stray calls.
Katy: We saw similar when developers used .callTimeout on the client vs per-request timeout. If an interceptor blocks the thread (heavy work) it can prevent timeouts from firing.
Lena: Minimal repro snippet I used (Flow collector):
```kotlin
suspend fun streamEvents(): Flow<String> = flow {
  val resp = retrofitService.stream().awaitResponse() // suspend
  resp.body?.source()?.let { src ->
    while (!src.exhausted()) { emit(src.readUtf8Line() ?: break) }
  }
}
```
The suspend never returns when server closes.
Marco: Two fixes: 1) use Call.timeout() per request so OkHttp enforces deadline even if interceptors block, e.g. `call.timeout().timeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`, 2) use `suspendCancellableCoroutine` wiring and ensure `invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() }` so coroutine cancellation cancels the call and resumes the collector.
Jun: Also prefer `source.readUtf8LineStrict()` with proper EOF handling? But careful: strict will throw on EOF. Better to loop on `readUtf8Line()` and break.
Katy: Action items for SDK: - add sample showing proper Flow + OkHttp Call wiring; - update retrofit suspend adapter to use cancellable pattern and preserve Call.timeout usage when available; - add a small integration test that starts streaming, force-close server socket, and assert collector completes.
QA-Bot: scheduled canary test: streaming-timeout-lane on emulator API 29/31.
Lena: Thanks. I'll push a patch to sample-apps with the corrected pattern and a short note about call vs client timeouts. :thumbsup:
